findings.text: ACPI mapping service resolves a physical range against firmware memory descriptors and produces an input output mapping with protection chosen from descriptor kind and attributes, defaulting to device semantics when no descriptor covers the request.

Mapping refuses requests spanning descriptor boundaries and refuses overlap with kernel memory, with a narrow allowance for kernel memory covered by a single non mapped reservation used for table overrides; reclaimable firmware memory already in the linear map is served by that mapping; executable firmware code never receives a writable mapping.

Error claim service preserves masking state, enters error context, delegates to firmware error notification, then either runs deferred work promptly when the interrupted context permits interrupts or reports deferral, before restoring prior masking.
Reservation helper excludes an ACPI address range from the linear map.
Presence helpers mark a logical CPU present or not present; mapping propagates an incoming negative identifier as failure with a one time diagnostic, otherwise succeeds.

Identity helpers expose per CPU firmware interrupt identity and reverse lookup from firmware identity to logical CPU by linear scan, reporting invalid identifier when out of range or not found and missing device when per CPU data is unavailable.

NUMA helpers expose early per CPU node assignments, populate them by parsing firmware affinity records, and record parsed proximity domains; disabled tables or disabled records cause entries to be skipped.

Early CPU to node table starts unassigned for every possible CPU; affinity handling validates record length, requires the enabled flag, translates proximity domain to node, ignores identities with no possible CPU, and treats node exhaustion as table error.

Parking mailbox comprises an identifier field, a reserved field and an entry address field; per CPU bookkeeping holds a mapped mailbox pointer, raw mailbox address, protocol version and firmware CPU number, with one entry per possible CPU.

Mailbox identifier is 32 bits and entry address is 64 bits, exchanged in little endian regardless of kernel endianness; firmware readiness is shown by an all ones identifier; mailbox storage uses device mapping semantics distinct from the nominal protocol attribute.
Parking setup records raw mailbox address, version and firmware CPU number from firmware interrupt description; validity requires both a nonzero address and a nonzero version.

Parking boot maps the mailbox, verifies the firmware readiness sentinel, stashes the mapping, publishes secondary entry address and CPU number, then signals the target; mapping failure or unexpected sentinel aborts without signaling; post boot on the awakened CPU warns if firmware did not clear the entry address.

Parking protocol publishes a CPU operations table binding initialization, preparation, boot and post boot handlers; initialization and preparation are no operation successes while boot and post boot implement the mailbox handshake.
Wakeup helper delivers a scheduler rescheduling interrupt to the target CPU as the wake mechanism and tolerates spurious deliveries.

Alternative region is a half open interval of descriptors delimited by begin and end pointers; progress uses a volatile system wide completion flag plus per capability applied bookkeeping intersected with system capabilities.

Alternative descriptors encode original and replacement locations as offsets from their own fields and encode capability plus optional callback selection in one field; helpers derive true pointers and separate capability from selector.

A branch targeting inside its own replacement sequence is left unchanged while branches leaving the sequence have displacement recomputed; page base addressing is rebased from replacement to original location; literal based addressing is unsupported and faults.

Instruction utilities provide branch displacement extraction and installation across unconditional, compare conditional and test bit families, generic immediate extraction and installation across multiple widths, and page base offset extraction and installation.

Immediate handling treats a split address field specially and otherwise uses a width to position table; unknown encodings report an error and yield a fault encoding or zero; encoding preserves all non immediate bits.

Core patch engine visits a region and applies only descriptors whose capability is both requested and present; callback descriptors must have empty payload while direct descriptors require equal original and replacement lengths; direct patching writes transformed instructions to a linear alias for core code and in place for modules, then performs cache maintenance and barrier sequencing and updates applied bookkeeping only for core code.

Boot patching runs on the boot CPU with boot capabilities; system wide patching handles dynamic shared object content first then suspends the machine while the boot CPU applies remaining capabilities and secondaries wait on the completion flag before a synchronization barrier; module patching applies all capabilities to the module region alone.
Callback helper fills the destination sequence with no operation instructions.
Capability query reports whether a given capability has been applied and rejects out of range capability numbers.

Patching faults on literal using replacements, mismatched direct lengths, nonempty callback payloads, unhandled branch families and module callbacks outside core text; capability queries warn on out of range values; post boot mailbox validation warns if firmware did not clear the entry address.

Firmware mapping warns and fails when a request spans descriptors or touches kernel memory; short affinity headers or node exhaustion mark the affinity table bad; mailbox boot fails when mapping is impossible or the readiness sentinel is absent.

No spinlock or mutex appears; core patching relies on early execution or stopped machine with secondaries spinning on a volatile flag; error claim sequencing relies on saved mask restoration paired with nonmaskable and interrupt entry and exit.

Each subsystem defines a fixed logging prefix and the deprecated instruction module enables tracepoint creation; core cache maintenance derives line size from the architectural cache type register and uses clean and invalidate to point of coherency followed by barrier, full instruction cache invalidation and synchronization.
Core patch region limits come from linker provided section boundaries and the region descriptor lives in initialization only storage.
